title: fix(plugin-auth): every in-process auth bridge hands handleRequest the request's transport
body:
Fixes #24877

Clause-②: no

## What changes

`AuthManager.handleRequest(request, transport?)` establishes a request's client address by the platform's client-address trust rule (ADR-0069 D5/D7, `resolveClientAddress`, `server.trustProxy`): forwarded headers only when the deployment declares a trusted proxy, the transport's peer address otherwise. Every in-process bridge in `auth-plugin.ts` that re-dispatches through `handleRequest` now judges the re-dispatched request on the same facts as the request it serves, on both branches of that rule:

- **The transport.** Each bridge hands `handleRequest` the transport of the request it serves, as the catch-all auth mount does (`transportOf(c)`).
- **The forwarding headers.** The six bridges whose helper rebuilds the request before re-dispatching it now carry the incoming request's forwarding headers onto it. The list is the rule's own, `FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS`. `resolveClientAddress` now iterates that same list, and the helpers copy it through one shared function, so no helper names a header itself. Without a declared trusted proxy, the rule ignores those headers and the re-dispatched request is judged on the connection peer. With one, it is judged on the forwarded client address.

| Bridge | How it reaches `handleRequest` | Transport | Forwarding headers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /admin/remove-user` | delegates the request itself | `handleRequest(c.req.raw, transportOf(c))` | already on the request |
| `POST /admin/has-permission` (delegate lane) | delegates the request itself | `handleRequest(c.req.raw, transportOf(c))` | already on the request |
| `POST /admin/sso/register` | `runRegisterSsoProviderFromForm(handle, …)` | `handle` is `handleWithTransportOf(c)` | `forwardAuthHeaders` (now also used here), and the session read |
| `POST /admin/sso/register-saml` | `runRegisterSamlProviderFromForm(handle, …)` | `handle` is `handleWithTransportOf(c)` | `forwardAuthHeaders` (now also used here), and the session read |
| `POST /admin/sso/request-domain-verification` | `runRequestDomainVerification(handle, …)` | `handle` is `handleWithTransportOf(c)` | `forwardAuthHeaders` |
| `POST /admin/sso/verify-domain` | `runVerifyDomain(handle, …)` | `handle` is `handleWithTransportOf(c)` | `forwardAuthHeaders` |
| `POST /send-verification-email` | `runResendVerificationEmail(handle, …)` | `handle` is `handleWithTransportOf(c)` | the session read and the send |
| `POST /sys-session/revoke` | `sysSessionRevokeDepsFor(manager, …)`, whose `handle` calls `manager.handleRequest` | the manager slice's `handleRequest` is `handleWithTransportOf(c)` | the owner lane's re-dispatch |

`handleWithTransportOf(c)` is one helper beside `gateAdmin`: `(request) => this.authManager!.handleRequest(request, transportOf(c))`. The list and the one copy function, `carryForwardedClientAddress(from, to)`, live in a new internal module, `client-address-forwarding.ts`. That module is import-free and is not on the package's `exports` map. Neither the package root nor the published `./client-address` entry re-exports it, so this PR adds no published export: the built `./client-address` entry still exports `resolveClientAddress` alone. `client-address.ts` imports the list for `resolveClientAddress`. The three helper modules call the shared function: twice in `register-sso-provider.ts` (`forwardAuthHeaders` and the session read), twice in `send-verification-email.ts` (the session read and the send), and once in `sys-session-revoke.ts` (the owner lane). The OIDC and SAML register builders were byte-identical to `forwardAuthHeaders` and now call it. `transportOf` and `handleRequest` are unchanged. `resolveClientAddress` decides exactly as before: it reads `X-Forwarded-For`, then `X-Real-IP`, now from the list rather than from two literals.

### The eighth bridge

The card lists seven sites, from `git grep -n "handleRequest(" -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`. `POST /sys-session/revoke` is an eighth. Its owner lane re-dispatches through `handleRequest` one hop away, inside `sysSessionRevokeDepsFor` (`sys-session-revoke.ts`: `handle: (request) => manager.handleRequest(request)`), so that grep does not list it. It is the same rule and the same mechanical fix, so it is fixed here. The mount hands the factory a manager slice whose `handleRequest` carries the transport. The seat accepted it and amended the claim's surface.

## Pins

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/bridge-redispatch-transport.pin.test.ts` uses the D5/D7 real-mount fixture from `client-address-vendor-trust-rule.test.ts`: `AuthPlugin.registerAuthRoutes` on a real Hono app in front of a real `AuthManager` on the installed better-auth, with the peer on `c.env.incoming`. It runs two deployments: one declaring no trusted proxy, one declaring `trustProxy`. Each pin reads the client address carried by every request the bridge hands the vendored library's handler. That address is the platform-owned header `handleRequest` writes from the address it established. The bridge's own inner route must be among those requests, so a bridge that never reached the library cannot pass vacuously. Every request also carries the platform-owned header naming another address, and on neither branch may it decide anything.

No trusted proxy declared (the caller's forwarding headers name another address):

- control: a request through the catch-all is judged on its connection peer
- a request through ROUTE is judged on its connection peer when no trusted proxy is declared, once for each of the eight bridges

A trusted proxy declared (the connection peer is the proxy hop; each pin sends `X-Forwarded-For` and, separately, `X-Real-IP`):

- control: a request through the catch-all is judged on the forwarded client address
- a request through ROUTE is judged on the forwarded client address when a trusted proxy is declared, once for each of the eight bridges

Legs A to C ran at `486e46d1b`; `auth-plugin.ts` and the pin file are byte-identical at this PR's head. Legs D to G ran at this PR's head, `fbd92ad31`. Each restore was proven: blob equals HEAD's, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the tree is clean. The test imports its subjects from `src/`, so no `dist/` sits on the path.

| Leg | Forbidden behaviour put back | Red (`Tests N failed \| M passed (28)`) |
|---|---|---|
| A | `handleWithTransportOf` drops the transport | 6: the no-trust pins of sso/register, sso/register-saml, request-domain-verification, verify-domain, send-verification-email and sys-session/revoke |
| B | the two delegate sites drop `transportOf(c)` (2 hits) | 2: the no-trust pins of remove-user and has-permission |
| C | the revoke mount goes back to `sysSessionRevokeDepsFor(this.authManager!, basePath)` | 1: the no-trust pin of sys-session/revoke |
| D | `register-sso-provider.ts` stops calling the shared copy (2 calls) | 4: the trusted-proxy pins of sso/register, sso/register-saml, request-domain-verification and verify-domain |
| E | `send-verification-email.ts` stops calling it (2 calls) | 1: the trusted-proxy pin of send-verification-email |

| G | the shared `carryForwardedClientAddress` copies nothing | 6: the trusted-proxy pins of the six helper bridges |

Every other pin, and both controls, stayed green in every leg.

## Acceptance notes

- `sysSessionRevokeDepsFor` could take the transport itself. That edit lands in the factory's signature, outside this card's surface. The slice keeps the transport change in `auth-plugin.ts`.
- `IAuthService.handleRequest(request)` in the spec contract has no transport parameter, and two callers outside `plugin-auth` hand the request alone. Their reach is unmeasured, and both sit in landings this card excludes. Carrier: none.
- No new gate. The pins sit beside the code, and a bridge added later is covered only when its PR pins it.
